title: Resume-awareness prompts, context re-read, and worktree-safe runtime isolation
summary: Make resume-required awareness explicit in recap/task-start flows, require context re-read when resuming active work, and isolate volatile runtime state across worktrees and branches.
description: This phase follows the resume/deviation behavior introduced around `packages/plan-core/src/task-selection.ts`, `packages/plan-core/src/recap.ts`, `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts`, `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts`, and the Web UI focus surfaces in `packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/layout/app-shell.tsx` plus task detail routes. Current implementation knows about `resume-required` / `pendingResume`, but it treats them mostly as advisory display text or optional warnings: the recap prints a resume advisory, `task_start` can honor an explicit start while only appending warning text, and a task already `in-progress` can be resumed in practice without forcing a fresh read of parent feature/phase descriptions. Additionally, runtime state such as resume awareness and active session context must remain safe when the same planner is consumed from multiple worktrees, branches, or cloned folders; work on one feature/phase must not create unnecessary conflicts for another branch or worktree. This phase defines the boundary between shared planner state and local runtime/session state, ensures every recap and task-entry flow proposes outstanding resume-required work explicitly without hard-blocking it, extends the protocol so agents must re-read feature/phase/task context when re-entering already in-progress work even if no `task_start` occurs, and verifies the whole behavior with cross-worktree / cross-branch isolation tests. Preserve harness-agnostic core behavior, avoid introducing new global planner hotspots, prefer feature-local or phase-local writes over shared root churn, and keep canonical workflow status separate from resume markers in the UI.

acceptedDecisions.title: Resume-required is mandatory awareness, not a hard block
acceptedDecisions.decision: Outstanding resume-required work must always be proposed explicitly after recap and before task-entry decisions, but it must not hard-block starting other work when the user chooses to continue elsewhere.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: The current advisory-only rendering allows agents to forget pending resume context, while a hard denial would be too rigid for real operational flow. The correct behavior is explicit awareness plus user choice.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Update recap and task-entry flows so they surface a visible resume proposal and checkpoint context every time resume-required work exists. Preserve explicit user override and keep canonical workflow status separate from resume markers.

acceptedDecisions.title: Runtime resume awareness must be safe across worktrees and branches
acceptedDecisions.decision: Volatile runtime/session awareness for resume and task re-entry must avoid shared planner hotspots and be isolatable per worktree or equivalent local context, while canonical planner entities remain mergeable across branches and folders.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Multiple worktrees, branches, or cloned folders may work on different features/phases concurrently. Shared runtime state in global planner files creates unnecessary conflicts and breaks safe parallel consumption.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Define shared-vs-local storage boundaries in core, prefer local overlay state under `.planner/.local/*` for session/runtime awareness, and verify at least feature-level isolation with tests, ideally phase-level where achievable.

acceptedDecisions.title: Remove paused from canonical lifecycle statuses
acceptedDecisions.decision: Tasks, phases, features, and requirements must not use a canonical `paused` workflow status. Resume checkpoints stay in `pauseSnapshot`/`workDeviations`, while the task lifecycle remains on canonical statuses such as `planned` and `in-progress`. Header/focus surfaces must list only live checkpointed or resume-required work, never resumed or terminal tasks.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Introducing `paused` as a canonical status broke consumers that assumed the historical lifecycle set, including the real Pi adapter dist path used by the user. Keeping checkpoint state separate preserves resume semantics without making task trees, lists, filters, and adapters silently drop tasks or miscompute activity.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Schema/type unions remove `paused`; core normalizes legacy persisted `paused` tasks back to `planned` with checkpoint metadata preserved; pause/resume APIs now save and restore checkpoints without persisting a separate status; `/tasks/focus`, Pi, MCP, and Web UI only surface live `pendingResume` work from active checkpoints/deviations and exclude resumed/done targets.

acceptedDecisions.title: T299 runtime-deviation storage split (.local/backups-free)
acceptedDecisions.decision: Resume-awareness runtime state (workDeviations) moves from shared .planner/project.json into worktree-local .planner/.local/deviations.json. plan-core loadProject() returns a read-view merge so all existing readers (recap.ts, serve.ts /tasks/focus, web-ui loader.ts, loadProject().workDeviations assertions) keep working unchanged; mutations (addWorkDeviation/setWorkDeviationState/pruneObsoleteWorkDeviations) and init seed .local; saveProject() strips workDeviations and api.ts updateProject() strips it from the PUT /project body, so project.json workDeviations stays [] and never churns across worktrees/branches. A one-time idempotent copy-then-clear migration runs lazily inside loadProject() for legacy projects, preserving all deviation data.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: project.json carries createdAt/updatedAt and is shared across git worktrees/branches; persisting per-session runtime state (task-switch deviations, pauseSnapshot, resume-required markers) there causes timestamp churn and cross-branch merge conflicts. The .local/ transient root (already home to resume.json, allocations/, backups/, tmp/) is the documented worktree-local home; rules.json is a static code constant (T304), so deviations are the remaining runtime state to relocate. Readers must not change to minimize cross-harness (Pi/MCP/server/Web UI) blast radius.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: plan-store.ts: deviationsPath()/loadWorkDeviations()/saveWorkDeviations() at 956-971; loadProject migration+merge at 1191-1203; saveProject strip at 2063; addWorkDeviation@2010, setWorkDeviationState@2021, pruneObsoleteWorkDeviations@716-725 all use .local; init seeds .local/deviations.json=[] @1062-1064. api.ts: updateProject strips PUT body @165-167. Verified: pnpm check + web-ui check clean; plan-core 193/9 (0 new failures); plan-mcp+pi-adapter integration 51/0; mkdtemp migration+read-view+no-churn smoke PASS. Live migration is lazy (runs on first loadProject with rebuilt code) and safe; verified only in throwaway mkdtemp per no-live-mutation rule.

tasks.title: Propose outstanding resume-required work after recap and before task start
tasks.description:
Update the recap and explicit task-start flows in `packages/plan-core/src/recap.ts`, `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts`, and `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts` so outstanding resume-required work is always proposed explicitly to the agent/user after the initial recap and again before starting a different task. Current behavior only prints advisory text such as "Resume advisory" while still honoring explicit starts, which allows the agent to forget the pending resume context. Keep the behavior advisory rather than blocking: the user must still be able to continue with different work, but the flow must force awareness and a visible proposal to resume first. Preserve existing distinction between active conflict denial, priority recommendation, and resume-required awareness.

---
**Completion summary:**
Implemented P069(F005)/T296 — explicit resume-required proposal in the explicit task-start flow (both adapters), advisory/non-blocking.

Root behavior before: when an agent started a DIFFERENT task while a resume-required was pending, both `task_start` (Pi, packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts ~4241) and `planner-task-start` (MCP, packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts ~1272) emitted only a trailing one-line "⚠️ Resume advisory" — easy to ignore, not machine-readable.

Changes:
1. packages/plan-core/src/task-selection.ts — added `buildResumeRequiredProposal({ref,title,taskId,phaseId,snapshot})` returning `{ text, structured }` (the structured form mirrors the existing `task_complete`/`task_update` `resumeRequired` payload). Pure, harness-agnostic, additive (no change to `recommendNextTask`).
2. pi-adapter/src/index.ts task_start — when `selection.kind === "resume" && selection.candidate.task.id !== task.id`: build `resumeProposal` (ref via formatPhaseRef, snapshot from task.pauseSnapshot or the resume-required/resolved deviation snapshot), replace the weak advisory with the explicit "↩️ RESUME REQUIRED before starting a different task: <ref> — <title> … Next action: task_start <ref> … Explicit task request honored" block, and return `resumeRequired: resumeProposal.structured` alongside `details`. Start still succeeds (advisory).
3. plan-mcp/src/index.ts planner-task-start — identical, returning `resumeRequired` via writeAndSummarize's structuredContent.
4. recap.ts left unchanged — it already proposes resume-required explicitly after recap (pendingResume block), satisfying the "after recap" half; this task strengthens the "before task start" half.

Tests: updated packages/pi-adapter/test/mutations.test.mjs and packages/plan-mcp/test/mcp-crud.test.mjs skipAdvisory assertions to require the structured `resumeRequired` proposal + the new explicit text while the requested task still starts. Full suites: pi-adapter 47/47, plan-mcp 50/50, core check clean.

Note: packages/plan-core/test/task-selection.test.mjs has a pre-existing failing assertion (recommendNextTask returns 'none' instead of 'resume') caused by the uncommitted T253 "normalized outcomes" branch work in recommendNextTask (paused→checkpointed refactor); unrelated to this change (T296 only added helper functions). No commit made (project rules).

tasks.title: Add cross-worktree and resume-protocol isolation tests
tasks.description:
Add verification for the new work-resumption protocol and storage boundaries using tests around `packages/plan-core`, adapters, server contracts, and any fixture infrastructure needed for multiple worktrees or cloned planner directories. The suite must prove that resume-required proposals remain visible across recap/task-entry flows, that re-entering already in-progress work triggers the required context awareness, and that concurrent work on different features/phases from separate worktrees or branches does not create avoidable planner conflicts. Prefer tests that exercise real persisted planner state with isolated temporary roots/worktrees over mocks, and verify at least feature-level isolation, with phase-level isolation where the implementation makes it possible.

---
**Completion summary:**
Implemented P069(F005)/T297 — cross-worktree and resume-protocol isolation tests.

Deliverable: NEW packages/plan-core/test/resume-protocol-isolation.test.mjs (6 tests, all passing) exercising real persisted planner state in isolated temp roots/worktrees. Three areas:

1. Resume-required visibility across recap flows (harness-agnostic buildRecap, same core feeds Pi + MCP):
   - recap surfaces a pending resume-required task with `Current focus: resume required — P001(F001)/T01 — task 1 (planned)` + `Resume advisory` (pi harness).
   - same assertion for mcp harness.
   - no resume-required text when nothing is pending.
   - completing the resume target clears its live deviations AND keeps shared project.json free of runtime state (workDeviations:[]).

2. Re-entry context awareness: a pending resume-required recap tells the agent to `Read its checkpoint before deciding` and carries the target ref `P001(F001)/T01`, satisfying the "re-read feature/phase/task context when re-entering in-progress work" requirement.

3. Cross-worktree runtime-state isolation (T299 boundary): cloning canonical planner data into a second worktree while EXCLUDING `.planner/.local` yields a worktree that does NOT see the first worktree's resume-required deviation (runtime state isolated per worktree); each worktree owns its own runtime state without affecting the other. Proves concurrent work on different features/phases from separate worktrees creates no avoidable planner conflicts.

Also (user-authorized live cleanup, "1. sistema"): resolved 2 stale `resume-required` deviations in the live `.planner/.local/deviations.json` (ids 77aed945…, 7d4923d0…) that pointed at T299 after it was completed — leftover task_switch checkpoints, never cleared on completion. Now 0 resume-required, audit preserved (4 total: 2 resolved, 2 resumed). This is why the live UI no longer shows T299 in the worktree/Resume Required section: T299 is `done` and the recap correctly excludes resume-required deviations whose target task is no longer planned/waiting/in-progress.

No source-code changes (T297 is test-only + the authorized live data cleanup). Verification: T297 file 6/6; core 200/209 (9 pre-existing T253 branch failures in task-selection.test.mjs, unchanged); pi-adapter 47/47; plan-mcp 50/50. No commit (project rules).

tasks.title: Define shared-vs-local planner runtime boundaries
tasks.description:
Map the runtime data involved in resume awareness and active work entry across `packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts`, `packages/plan-core/src/schema.ts`, `.planner/project.json`, and `.planner/.local/*`. Current state mixes canonical planner data with volatile runtime/session concerns such as `workDeviations`, current focus, resume prompts, and local activity context. Define which data must remain shared and mergeable across branches/worktrees versus which data must become worktree-local or derivable at runtime. The output must explicitly cover resume-required markers, task-entry awareness, current focus/session context, and any advisory bookkeeping needed so two worktrees working on different features/phases do not create unnecessary conflicts. Preserve harness-agnostic core semantics and document invariants that downstream adapters and UI can rely on.

---
**Completion summary:**
Implemented P069(F005)/T298 — define shared-vs-local planner runtime boundaries.

Deliverable: NEW packages/plan-core/docs/runtime-boundaries.md (authoritative spec of the shared vs worktree-local boundary + the invariants every harness relies on) plus a one-line pointer comment at PlanStore.localRoot() (packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts:947) linking to the doc.

Content of the doc:
- Principle: canonical planner data in `.planner/` is shared+mergeable; volatile runtime/session state in `.planner/.local/` is worktree-local, git-ignored, never merged.
- Shared/mergeable table: manifest.json, project.json (counters + rules/scope/decisions; workDeviations always []/absent after T299), features/, phases/, tasks/, requirements.json, handoffs/, rules.json (static, timestamp-free).
- Worktree-local table: deviations.json (resume-required stack, T299), resume.json (per-session focus + guard-bypass), activity.json, timestamp.json, generated/, backups/, tmp/, handoff-archive/ (terminal-phase auto-archive).
- 8 invariants adapters/UI rely on: (1) canonical status is sole source of truth, resume markers derived; (2) loadProject().workDeviations is a merged read-view, writers use addWorkDeviation/setWorkDeviationState/pruneObsoleteWorkDeviations, saveProject strips workDeviations; (3) resume-required derived at read time and excludes done targets; (4) counters stay shared (never localize); (5) resume.json/activity.json machine-local; (6) handoff archive local; (7) read-view merge is the single integration contract (recap/buildRecap, serve /tasks/focus, recommendNextTask); (8) proposing resume is advisory, standardized via buildResumeRequiredProposal.
- Cross-worktree isolation section (matches the T297 test).
- Open items: webPort shared-by-convenience (not a merge conflict); entity timestamps shared (inherent canonical-data conflicts, out of scope).

No functional code changes — the boundary already exists (T299 relocated deviations to .local; T304 made rules.json static/timestamp-free). This task documents the contract so future adapters/UI and other projects consuming the extensions rely on stable invariants. Core check clean. No commit (project rules).

Note on ordering: no task reorder was needed — the only dependency inversion (T297 tests ← T299 impl) was moot because T299 was already done, so the sequence T296→T297→T298→T258 had no live inversion. Optionally the intended dependency order (T298 design → T299 impl → T297 tests) can be recorded as a phase note for future readers.

tasks.title: Move resume-awareness runtime state to worktree-local storage
tasks.description:
Implement the storage split decided for this phase by moving or deriving resume-awareness/session-specific runtime state out of shared planner hotspots and into worktree-local state under `.planner/.local/*` or equivalent infrastructure in `packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts`. Current state risks coupling runtime awareness to shared files such as `.planner/project.json`, which is unsafe when multiple worktrees, branches, or cloned folders consume the same planner. Ensure the resulting design keeps canonical feature/phase/task data mergeable, avoids introducing new root-level churn, and remains consumable by Pi, MCP, server, and Web UI surfaces without breaking existing planner semantics.

---
**Completion summary:**
T299 done. Implemented the resume-awareness storage split: runtime workDeviations now live in worktree-local .local/deviations.json (plan-core plan-store.ts: deviationsPath/loadWorkDeviations/saveWorkDeviations @956-971; addWorkDeviation @2010, setWorkDeviationState @2021, pruneObsoleteWorkDeviations @716 all write .local; loadProject @1191 does one-time copy-then-clear migration from project.json then returns a read-view merge; saveProject @2063 strips workDeviations:[] to prevent shared-file churn; init @1062 seeds .local/deviations.json=[]). plan-web-ui api.ts @165 strips workDeviations from the PUT /project body so the editor cannot round-trip runtime state. No other readers changed (recap.ts, serve.ts /tasks/focus, web-ui loader.ts, loadProject().workDeviations assertions all read the merged .local view). Verified: pnpm check (tsc -b) + web-ui check clean; plan-core 193/9 (9 pre-existing T253 failures, 0 new; deviation tests pass); plan-mcp + pi-adapter integration 51/0 pass; mkdtemp migration + read-view + no-churn smoke test PASS. No commit (project rules). Live migration is lazy+safe (runs on next loadProject with rebuilt code); not run against the live .planner per no-live-mutation policy — verified in throwaway mkdtemp instead.
tasks.notes:
## Visibility root cause #2 — legacy "paused" status breaks loading (FIXED 2026-08-21)

**Symptom:** after restart, P069/T299/T253 not visible in Web UI, even via search. Two stale `pi` processes were running: 54532 on :56321 (OLD bundle B97B4wii) and 82542 on :51556 (NEW bundle but incomplete in-memory load: 67 phases, P069 404).

**Real root cause (deeper than the bundle staleness):** removing canonical `"paused"` from the Zod enums meant any persisted `statusLog` entry with `fromStatus`/`toStatus` = `"paused"` (or `task.status` = `"paused"`) failed `PhaseSchema` validation **at read time, before** `normalizeTasks` could rewrite it. `loadAllPhases()` swallows per-phase errors (`catch { /* skip corrupted files */ }`), so the whole phase was silently dropped. P069 had such an entry in `tasks.[4].statusLog`. The old dist tolerated `"paused"` (still in enum), hence 68 phases there; the new dist dropped P069 → 67.

**Fix:** `packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts` — `readJson()` now runs `migrateLegacyStatuses()` (maps `"paused"`→`"planned"` on `status`/`fromStatus`/`toStatus` fields) on the parsed JSON **before** `schema.parse`. Safe because `"paused"` is fully removed from the domain; normalized value persists on next save. Rebuilt `@agent-plan/core` + `@agent-plan/pi-adapter`.

**Verified:** `loadAllPhases()` → 68 phases, P069 present, zero `"paused"` remaining. `loadAll()` loads cleanly.

**Stale tests aligned to checkpoint model (rename debt):** `packages/plan-core/test/task-pause.test.mjs` (status `planned`, displayStatus `planned`, `fromStatus planned`, `/cannot be checkpointed from planned/`) and `packages/plan-core/test/recap.test.mjs` (`checkpoint to evaluate`, `Saved checkpoints`, `with checkpoints`, standalone-list labels `Why:`/`Checkpoint:`/`How:`). `node --test` on these 3 files: 22/22 pass.

**Required user action:** quit BOTH stale pi processes (54532 on :56321 and 82542 on :51556) and start ONE fresh `pi --no-extensions -e packages/pi-adapter/dist/index.js`. The new dist loads all 68 phases (P069, T299, T253 visible) and serves the fresh bundle. Do not point the browser at :56321 until it is the fresh single session.

**Not committed** (per workflow: no commit without explicit approval). Working tree on feature/p059-t253-normalized-outcomes.

tasks.title: Require feature and phase re-read when resuming already in-progress work
tasks.description:
